exposure: low maternal and paternal education level
cohort: 285 children (95 with developmental delay and 190 randomly selected controls)
finding: Maternal age ≥ 35 years, low maternal education level, consanguineous marriage, and delivery by cesarean section were associated with an increased risk of developmental delay in early childhood.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of developmental delay in early childhood.
